cases.question: What is the procedure for a production rollback?
cases.answer:
The procedure for a production rollback involves pausing the deployment pipeline, selecting the previous healthy image digest, and redeploying that image. [S1]

After redeploying the previous healthy image, the health endpoint and error dashboard must be verified for ten minutes. [S1]

In case of a rollback, the on-call engineer must be notified and the failed release's logs attached to the incident ticket. [S1]

cases.question: When can routine production deployments happen?
cases.answer: Routine production deployments happen on weekdays between 09:00 and 16:00 UTC. [S1]

cases.question: What is the on-call escalation process?
cases.answer:
Page the on-call engineer when the error rate exceeds five percent for five consecutive minutes. [S1] [S5]

The primary on-call engineer must acknowledge a production page within five minutes. [S2]

If the primary on-call engineer does not acknowledge within five minutes, page the secondary on-call engineer. [S2]

If no engineer acknowledges within ten minutes of the first page, escalate to the engineering manager. [S2]

The first responding engineer acts as incident commander until ownership is explicitly handed over. [S2]

Publish a status update every fifteen minutes until recovery. [S2]

Never include customer records, access tokens, or private debugging output in status updates. [S2]

The incident scribe maintains a timeline of decisions in the incident ticket. [S2]

An incident is resolved after the customer-facing service has been healthy for thirty consecutive minutes. [S2]

A blameless postmortem is due within three business days of resolution for every SEV1 and SEV2 incident. [S2]
